correctness.rationale: PASS. The exact model is symmetric positive definite because its quadratic form is a sum of unit-edge differences and strictly positive pinned energies. Its Lyapunov equation yields Sigma=A^{-1}/2 with the stated white-noise normalization. Splitting the hub from the independent leaves and applying the inverse Schur complement gives trace=s1+(1+s2)/tau; tau_C=kappa(kappa+q)/(1+kappa) and tau_L=q*kappa/(1+kappa) are positive for every admissible parameter. Algebraic subtraction exactly yields the displayed rational difference. All q-subsets are covered by two leaf-permutation orbits; positivity of the denominator makes the sign a complete global test. f(kappa)=kappa/(1+kappa)^2 reaches its unique 1/4 maximum at kappa=1 and is invariant under reciprocal gain, establishing every strict/tie phase. n=7 q=3 yields roots 2±sqrt(3), J_C=31/8 and J_L=23/6 at gain one. The packaged standard-library checker directly inverts rational matrices and reproduces 1455 comparisons. It is a finite regression test; the all-n claim relies on the displayed algebra, not enumeration.

originality.rationale: PASS with residual historical uncertainty. arXiv:1302.0450v2 exactly formulates the stochastic finite-feedback trace-inverse selection problem and develops generic algorithms, but does not state its exact every-budget star minimizer. arXiv:1407.1569v2 treats one/two noisy leaders and any number of noise-free leaders, not an arbitrary number of finitely pinned star leaders; arXiv:1708.06873v1 likewise solves noisy pairs on cycles and noise-free tree cases. arXiv:1804.10818v2 contains a single-pinned-star proposition but minimizes a grounded smallest eigenvalue, not the full finite-gain trace inverse. The new substantive claim is the complete hub-versus-leaf finite-gain phase classification, including first reentrant 7-node witness and reciprocal transition gains; the stochastic covariance formula and Schur complement are acknowledged as established background. Comparisons with the inspected primary literature and public mathematical records found no equivalent. Priority outside reviewed literature cannot be ruled out.
residual_risks: A historically unindexed paper could have specialized the generic finite-gain objective to stars or derived a mathematically equivalent threshold.
General trace-inverse leader-selection methods might imply the theorem following additional graph-specific algebra; the explicit classification is not claimed to be a new objective or inversion tool.

value.rationale: PASS. Leader location is a central network-design decision in noisy consensus with finite feedback, and an exact optimum is valuable even for a canonical graph family. The result supplies a global placement decision for every star order, leader budget, and feedback gain, identifies a sharp previously nonobvious boundary, and shows that increasing stabilizing feedback can optimally REMOVE then RESTORE hub participation. The smallest concrete realization has n=7, q=3 and algebraic reciprocal thresholds 2±sqrt(3); there is no such reentrance for one or two leaders. This is a meaningful structural phase classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice or general formula restatement. The theorem is limited to homogeneous finite gains, unit stars, and the specified total steady-state variance; no extension to other graph classes or costs is asserted.
